title: Region lock enforcement lifecycle notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick working notes to capture a proposed enforcement lifecycle for region locks (what we also call region locks / region anchors) across hosted/dedicated/private. Focus is operational: feature flags, metrics to watch, rollback triggers, operator steps, and short example customer messages. This is intentionally informal — meant to be the canonical draft we iterate on before formalizing into a playbook.

Background/context:
- We need a predictable, low-risk path to turn on region enforcement for customers who contract for data-to-region guarantees. Enforcement must be reversible and observable.
- Previous artifacts cover routing, pinning, and legal requirements; this doc focuses on the flip side: staged enforcement and how to back out safely when telemetry or customer impact appears.

Definitions used here (quick):
- region lock: immutable constraint that tenant requests must route to resources within a specified region/jurisdiction.
- soft-enforcement: routing is biased to the locked region but fallbacks are allowed and recorded (used to measure compatibility and latent issues).
- hard-enforcement: routing refuses out-of-region execution unless explicit exception flag is set.
- caretakers: operators assigned to a tenant during the roll (SEs + SREs + legal point).

Lifecycle stages and rationale:
1) Preflight (feature flag off, audit-only)
   - Purpose: gather baseline distribution of requests, headers, third-party callbacks that may cross boundaries.
   - Actions: enable audit logs for tenant, add residency headers to traces, run agent that maps external callbacks to IP ranges.
   - Metrics: %requests already in-region, #out-of-region callbacks, list of dependent external endpoints.

2) Soft enforcement (feature flag: region-lock.soft = true)
   - Purpose: route preferentially to locked region but allow fallback. Track success/error deltas vs baseline.
   - Actions: set routing weight 95% to locked region, 5% fallback; enable anomaly alerting; notify customer stake-holders (email + CS slack channel).
   - What to watch: 99th percentile latency delta, increase in user errors (4xx/5xx), cache-miss rate, prefix cache warmup time.
   - Safety net: automatic revert to preflight if error rate > 1.5x baseline for > 10m.

3) Hard enforcement (feature flag: region-lock.hard = true)
   - Purpose: make enforcement binding while minimizing blast radius.
   - Actions: require explicit exemption tokens for whitelisted endpoints. Apply deny rule at routing tier. Enforce quota and SLA guardrails for eviction scenarios.
   - What to watch: total blocked requests, number of exception requests created, customer-reported failures.
   - Safety net: operator must acknowledge and create runbook ticket before enabling; emergency rollback command available to revert to soft.

4) Stabilization and audit (post-hard)
   - Purpose: ensure logs, telemetry, legal evidence are collected and packaged for contract compliance.
   - Actions: generate auditable bundle (request samples, routing evidence, timestamps, operator approvals). Verify KMS/HSM key residency where applicable.

Rollback scenarios and playflows (practical notes):
- Type A: transient latency spike after soft enable
  - Immediate action: enable automatic revert (feature-flag toggle) which sends traffic back to baseline distribution for that tenant.
  - Operator steps: collect traces for 2 minutes pre/post toggle, file postmortem.
- Type B: persistent functional error tied to third-party callback
  - Immediate action: revert to preflight, open escalation to SE and Solutions Eng. Create temporary exception for specific callback endpoint until patch.
  - Communication: notify customer with template below within 30 minutes.
- Type C: legal or contract ambiguity discovered
  - Immediate action: hard enforcement off, preserve evidence, notify legal and account team. Pause onboarding of new commits to tenant config.

Feature flags and config knobs (implementation-level):
- region-lock.mode = [off, audit, soft, hard] (single source-of-truth at region-routing service)
- region-lock.weight = integer (percentage traffic to pinned region during soft)
- region-lock.exception-list = list (CIDR or service-id) stored in customer profile w/ admin approvals
- region-lock-telemetry = true|false (enables extended trace headers and debug logs)
- emergency-revert-token = auto-generate ephemeral token operator must use when reverting from hard

Telemetry, alert thresholds, and dashboards to create before any roll:
- Dashboards: Tenants > Region lock > Success rate | Latency | Blocked requests | Exceptions created.
- Alerts (suggested):
  - Soft stage: error-rate > 1.5x baseline for 10m => auto-revert (P3 alert to oncall, notify customer comm channel).
  - Hard stage: blocked-requests > 0.5% of tenant traffic for 15m => P2 alert and page SRE.
  - Any stage: unexpected increase in external callback failures => page SE oncall.

Operator runbook snippets (copy-paste friendly):
- To enable soft:
  1) SSH to routing-admin, set region-lock.mode=soft for tenant_id=X
  2) set region-lock.weight=95 for tenant_id=X
  3) add telemetry tag "rollout:v1" and post to #region-rollouts slack channel
- To revert to audit/off:
  1) flip region-lock.mode=audit 
  2) wait 2m, verify 95th latency returns to baseline, then set region-lock.mode=off if stable

Customer comm templates (short):
- Preflight notice (automated):
  Subject: Upcoming region residency test for your account
  Body: Hi <Account>, we will begin audit-only residency checks for your account on <date>. This will not change behavior but helps us prepare. Contact <AE> for questions.

- Soft rollout notice (SE-assisted):
  Subject: Beginning soft residency enforcement for <account> — monitoring closely
  Body: Hi <Account>, we will start preferential routing to your committed region tomorrow at <time>. We allow fallbacks and will monitor performance closely. Expect a follow-up within 24h with telemetry.

- Hard enforcement activation (legal+ops):
  Subject: Region-enforcement active for <account> as of <timestamp>
  Body: Hi <Account>, hard region enforcement is now enabled per contract. If you experience functional issues (failed callbacks, auth calls), open a support ticket referencing "region-exception" and we will triage.

Checklist before flipping any tenant to soft or hard:
- [ ] Audit logs enabled and sample captures verified
- [ ] Customer informed (AE or SE contacted)
- [ ] Runbook ticket created and caretakers assigned
- [ ] Dashboards and alerts provisioned for tenant
- [ ] Exception process documented and owner identified
- [ ] Legal sign-off for evidence collection (if required)

Open questions / tradeoffs to resolve:
- How long should soft-run remain in place before hard is allowed? (suggestion: minimum 48–72 hours of normal traffic and zero critical errors)
- Do we allow automatic per-tenant exception issuance via console or must exceptions be ticketed?
- Exact numerical alert thresholds need to be validated against historical tenant baselines; recommend running a 30-day simulation job.

Next immediate actions (owner assigned in parens):
- Draft a minimal telemetry dashboard template and JSON saved query (Ethan)
- Implement emergency-revert-token and document CLI flow (Liam)
- Draft customer email templates and share with legal for wording (Maya)
- Kick off 30-day simulation on staging with 20 demo tenants (SRE eng list)

Notes to self / friction points we've seen in past rolls:
- Hidden dependencies: webhooks to third-party transformers that are single-region cause silent failures; need a connector-scan step in preflight.
- Caching TTLs: long-tailed caches warmed in one region cause cold start faults when moved; prefer a staged cache priming job.
- Operator ergonomics: toggles must be reversible via UI and CLI, with recorded audit events.

If you're reading this and want to add a scenario or a comm-template, please edit and add notes — this is a living draft.

-- Sofia
